title: Frontend: PromiseAll With Concurrency Limit
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind PromiseAll With Concurrency Limit. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement async solution({values,limit}). Run lazy promise-producing jobs at most limit concurrently, each job resolves its value after one asynchronous turn. Return {values: input-order results,peak}. Invalid limit throws Invalid limit. Use actual promises; active work must remain bounded.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Promises already created may already be running, so accept factories.
alternativeApproaches: Propagate an AbortSignal and distinguish rejecting the aggregate promise from undoing work already sent to a server.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty tasks; limit one; limit above count.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
